meta.title: Authoritative API Contract Sheet — iroh P2P substrate
meta.compile_prompt_note: The compile prompt embedded JSON.stringify(good.map(x => x.contract)).slice(0, 60000), i.e. only the first 60,000 characters of the surviving-contract array. The complete surviving set was recovered from the workflow journal's structured results and cross-checked byte-for-byte by field/count against the 14 on-disk contracts/*.json files.

feature_constraints.quic-rpc: default-features = false, features = ["flume-transport"]; the iroh-transport feature MUST stay off (it pulls iroh ^0.35)
feature_constraints.iroh: default features (metrics, fast-apple-datapath, portmapper, tls-ring) are fine
feature_constraints.iroh-gossip: default net+metrics; iroh-docs 0.101.0 requires its net feature
feature_constraints.iroh-docs: default metrics, rpc, fs-store, redb-v2-migration are fine
feature_constraints.iroh-blobs: default hide-proto-docs, fs-store, rpc are fine

pinned_set.toolchain: Rust 1.91+ (iroh 1.5.0, iroh-blobs 0.105.0/0.103.1, iroh-docs 0.101.0, iroh-gossip 0.103.0/0.101.0 all declare rust_version 1.91; quic-rpc 0.20.0 declares 1.76). Witness build used rustc 1.98.1.
pinned_set.cargo_toml:
[dependencies]
iroh = "=1.5.0"
iroh-blobs = "=0.103.1"
iroh-docs = "=0.101.0"
iroh-gossip = "=0.101.0"
quic-rpc = { version = "=0.20.0", default-features = false, features = ["flume-transport"] }
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }

blockers.title: iroh-docs 0.101.0 excludes iroh-blobs 0.105.0 (the contracted blobs version)
blockers.detail: iroh-docs 0.101.0 declares iroh-blobs = "^0.103". For a 0.x crate, ^0.103 means >=0.103.0,<0.104.0, so 0.105.0 is outside the range. Cargo therefore resolves TWO copies (0.103.1 for docs, 0.105.0 for the direct dep). iroh_docs::engine::Engine::spawn takes iroh_blobs::api::Store and iroh_docs::protocol::Builder::spawn takes BlobsStore, so a 0.105.0 Store cannot be passed to a Docs built against 0.103.1. The 800-signatures sheet documents 0.105.0: those exact signatures are NOT usable in a single-version stack with iroh-docs 0.101.0.

evidence.what: live Cargo.lock contains both iroh-blobs 0.103.1 and 0.105.0
Engine::spawn / Builder::spawn signatures with iroh_blobs::api::Store / BlobsStore

blockers.resolution: Pin iroh-blobs = "=0.103.1" when iroh-docs 0.101.0 is in the graph. Accept that the sheet's 0.105.0 signatures then do not apply, or drop iroh-docs (no newer iroh-docs exists on crates.io).

blockers.title: iroh-docs 0.101.0 excludes iroh-gossip 0.103.0 (the contracted gossip version)
blockers.detail: iroh-docs 0.101.0 declares iroh-gossip = "^0.101.0" with features ["net"]; ^0.101.0 means >=0.101.0,<0.102.0. A direct iroh-gossip 0.103.0 dependency therefore resolves a second copy. iroh_docs::protocol::Builder::spawn(self, endpoint: Endpoint, blobs: BlobsStore, gossip: Gossip) and Engine::spawn(..., gossip: Gossip, ...) consume the 0.101.0 Gossip type, so a 0.103.0 Gossip will not type-check. Moreover 0.103.0 removed the rpc/rpc-tls-* features and irpc/noq dependencies that 0.101.0 has (surviving iroh-gossip contract), so the two APIs differ.

evidence.what: 0.103.0 features2: no rpc, no rpc-tls-ring/aws-lc-rs; deps have no irpc/noq
0.101.0 features2 includes rpc/rpc-tls-*, deps include irpc ^0.17 and noq ^1
live Cargo.lock contains both iroh-gossip 0.101.0 and 0.103.0

blockers.resolution: Pin iroh-gossip = "=0.101.0" for the five-crate set, and re-verify any gossip API used (this sheet documents 0.103.0). If 0.103.0 is mandatory, do not include iroh-docs 0.101.0.

blockers.title: irpc 0.17 vs irpc 1.0 split at the iroh-docs / iroh-blobs RPC boundary
blockers.detail: iroh-docs 0.101.0 and iroh-blobs 0.103.1 both require irpc ^0.17, while iroh-blobs 0.105.0 requires irpc ^1.0.0. Using the contracted blobs 0.105.0 with docs 0.101.0 resolves both irpc 0.17.0 and 1.0.0; irpc::Client<proto::Request> from one does not unify with the other. Store::from_client(client: impl Into<irpc::Client<proto::Request>>) in the 0.105.0 contract is the concrete boundary.

evidence.what: live Cargo.lock contains both irpc 0.17.0 and irpc 1.0.0

blockers.resolution: Use iroh-blobs 0.103.1 so the whole stack resolves a single irpc 0.17.0 (confirmed by the witness build).

blockers.title: quic-rpc 0.20.0 iroh-transport feature pins iroh ^0.35, incompatible with iroh 1.5.0
blockers.detail: quic-rpc 0.20.0 has an optional iroh dependency with req ^0.35, activated only by features2.iroh-transport = ["dep:iroh", ...]. Enabling it in an iroh 1.5.0 build resolves a second, 0.x iroh whose Endpoint/Connection types are unrelated to iroh 1.5.0's. quic-rpc 0.20.0 is otherwise transport-agnostic (default = flume-transport; quinn-transport uses the renamed iroh-quinn 0.13 dependency, not iroh).

evidence.what: 0.20.0 deps: iroh ^0.35 optional; features2.iroh-transport enables dep:iroh; default = flume-transport
quinn dep is package="iroh-quinn" version 0.13 renamed to quinn; no Message trait
independent corroboration: a 0.x iroh Connection cannot be handed to an iroh 1.x service without a port

blockers.resolution: Declare quic-rpc = { version = "=0.20.0", default-features = false, features = ["flume-transport"] } (or quinn-transport/hyper-transport) and never enable iroh-transport. For iroh-native RPC use irpc 0.17/1.0 or iroh's own ProtocolHandler instead.

blockers.title: Other surviving contracts that cannot be wired into an iroh 1.5.0 build
blockers.detail: iroh-roq 0.1.0 (the only published release) requires iroh ^0.33; its unpublished HEAD requires 0.35. iroh-dag-sync pins iroh = "1.0.0-rc.1", iroh-blobs = "0.102", iroh-gossip = "0.100" and is a binary-only experiment with no linkable library target. sendme 0.37.1 is binary-only (no src/lib.rs), so it is not a library dependency at all. These are hard blockers for including those contracts in the same iroh 1.5.0 stack, even though their own signatures were source-verified.

evidence.what: published 0.1.0 pins iroh 0.33; HEAD main pins 0.35 and is unpublished
experiment, bin-only, no lib target, no CRDT merge semantics

blockers.resolution: Keep these out of the pinned build; treat them as reference implementations, or vendor and port them to iroh 1.5.0.

blockers.title: iroh-blobs 0.103.0 is yanked; pin 0.103.1
blockers.detail: The crates.io sparse index marks iroh-blobs 0.103.0 yanked=true. iroh-docs 0.101.0's ^0.103 range therefore must be satisfied by 0.103.1 (unyanked, rust_version 1.91).
